summary.text: Samir Witta, an unaffiliated physician who says he has practiced oncology in Colorado for 25 years, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in Colorado's 6th District to Jason Crow.
He says he founded nonprofits aimed at helping patients with health costs.
He said he ran on health care costs, housing affordability, and limiting the influence of large donors.

paragraphs.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Witta came to the United States 27 years ago, and his first job was at a gas station in Washington, D.C. He earned an M.D. from Charles University in 1990 and a Ph.D. from the National Institutes of Health in 1995, and he graduated from the University of Colorado in 2004. His career experience is listed as physician.
Witta says he has practiced oncology in Colorado for 25 years and built his own clinic, and that 5280 Magazine has named him a top oncologist in the Denver metro area four years running.
He says he founded nonprofits to cover patients' insurance premiums, assembled a team to erase deductibles for cancer patients, and started organizations supporting youth sports and education.
He received 0.9% of the vote to Jason Crow's 65.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
